maya: Quick sync — thinking about adding a small "extension" to the hosting API so callers can express latency vs cost preference + soft-fallback semantics across hosted/dedicated/private. Draft below, want quick sanity check.
ashwin: Nice. can you show the shape?
maya: ```json
{
  "routing_preference": "latency",       // latency | cost | balanced
  "fallback_order": ["dedicated", "hosted"],
  "soft_fallback": true,                    // allow degraded QoS on fallback
  "data_residency": "strict",         // strict | best_effort
  "quota_reconciliation": "controlplane" // controlplane | caller-managed
}
```
ellie: Two quick calls out: (1) private deployments cannot fallback to hosted (policy/legal), so translation layer must reject/transform that. (2) need a explicit audit event when a fallback happens.
sophie: Concern: will exposing "cost" hints let external callers deduce our pricing or capacity tiers? we should keep the enum high-level.
maya: Agreed — the shape only exposes preference enums, not prices or capacity. runtime maps enums -> concrete routes.
kevin: We should also capture a tenant-level SLO intent so downstream billing/alerts can correlate: e.g. "latency_target_ms": 250 (optional).
ashwin: Edge case: dedicated pool saturated -> fallback to hosted might violate data_residency. we need a fail-open vs fail-closed decision. propose: if data_residency=strict then fallback must fail (no route).
ellie: +1. add a third enum for fallback_action: "allow" | "deny" | "escalate" (escalate -> create incident + try owner-approved route).
maya: Also propose a control-plane policy translation: private -> local runtime policy, dedicated -> prefer local pool, hosted -> routed through global gateway. We'll implement a PolicyTranslator component that enforces data_residency and maps soft_fallback into concrete admission rules.
infra-bot: Ticket INF-4182 created: "RoutingPreference V1 + PolicyTranslator"; assignee unassigned.
sophie: Must also add telemetry: metric labels like routing_reason, routed_from, routed_to, fallback_type. and an audit log entry for each translation decision.
kevin: Also add an evaluation harness: run synthetic traffic where dedicated saturates, private denies, hosted accepts — verify metrics and billing tags.
maya: Plan: I'll open RFC follow-up PR with the shape + translation semantics + e2e matrix. will include sample compiler/runtime mapping table (latency->nvlink optimize vs cost->batched quantized).
ashwin: I'll own runtime hookup (admission controller + admission counters).
ellie: I'll own the translation harness and private-policy tests.
sophie: I'll write the audit event schema and make sure it surfaces in Console. :thumbsup:
maya: Thanks — let's sync Fri 10:00 to lock API wording and whether "quota_reconciliation" defaults to controlplane or caller-managed.
kevin: adding brief note: ensure KMS/HSM flow doesn't change on fallback; if hosted route would require different KMS, block when data_residency=strict.
maya: Good call. adding to PR checklist.
